title: My Experience Shipping on Google Play and the App Store
author: MakingSoulStudio
selftext:
Last time I shared my failure story, and so many of you cheered me on. It really gave me strength. So this time I'd like to share my experience of successfully shipping a game, and the insights I picked up along the way.



While I was working on the slime project, an idea came to me.



I used to stream on a Korean platform called Spoon Radio, and back then my fans and I played a game as part of the show. Everyone got a secret name, and if someone said your secret name, you died. It was that simple.



I thought, wouldn't it be fun to turn this into a game that works like a group chat? So I made it. The UI design wasn't very hard, so I was able to ship it quickly.



But during the release, Codex and Claude Code both told me I needed a Mac environment to ship on iOS. I knew nothing about development, so I almost bought a MacBook.



Then a developer friend told me I didn't need one. So I went home and asked Claude again, and this time it agreed. All I needed was one test iPhone.



GitHub Actions can build, sign and deploy your iOS app on a cloud Mac. Basically you're borrowing a Mac through GitHub. On a private repo you get 200 free Mac minutes a month, and if you need more than that, you have to pay. You also need Apple's developer account, which is $99 a year.



The funny part is that the iOS release turned out to be the easy side. Apple has no closed test requirement. On Google Play, as a personal developer, I had to get 12 testers for 14 days, then production review took 4 days, then release review took another 14 days.



And making the game wasn't the end of it. I needed terms of service, a privacy policy, ads, payments and a way to report users. I had no idea about any of that. Making a game is definitely not one click.



So if you've been holding back on iOS because you don't have a MacBook, you don't need one. And double check what AI tells you, especially when it's about to cost you money.  


P.S. I'm a Korean developer. I write my posts myself but use AI to translate them, so please excuse anything that sounds awkward.
